blocks.title: Donors reducing ODA (24 largest of 25 in 2024/2025)

frames.text:
Based on official development assistance (grant equivalents in current US dollars) reported in OECD DAC1, 25 donor countries recorded a decrease in ODA from 2024 to 2025. Among DAC member countries, the following cut their ODA over this period: Australia, Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Japan, Lithuania, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, South Korea, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States.

(Note: Several non-DAC reporting countries, including Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Israel, Kuwait, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Malta, and Romania, also recorded cuts over this period.) The bar chart on the canvas displays the 24 largest donor cuts for the 2024 to 2025 period.

Counted as: grant equivalents (OECD headline), current USD · bilateral plus core contributions to multilaterals.

frames.text:

blocks.title: Difference in ODA in constant prices for donors reducing aid (24 largest of 34 in 2024/2025)
Germany ODA in constant prices, 2024 to 2025

frames.text:
Germany is not shown on the previous chart because of how the display cutoff selected the series. Display limit: across donors reporting to OECD DAC1, 34 countries recorded a decrease in constant-price ODA between 2024 and 2025. Because canvas charts can display at most 24 series, the chart automatically retained the 24 largest numerical values. Algebraic ordering of negative values: because aid reductions are negative numbers, the 24 largest values are the least negative (ranging from Estonia at -$1.71 million down to Poland at -$349 million). Donors with the largest cuts in magnitude, the most negative values such as Germany, fell into the bottom 10 and were cut from display. From OECD DAC1, Germany's official development assistance (grant equivalents in constant 2024 US dollars) was $32.8 billion in 2024 and $27.1 billion in 2025. Germany's ODA fell from 2024 to 2025.

Counted as: grant equivalents (OECD headline), constant 2024 USD · bilateral plus core contributions to multilaterals.

frames.text:
Based on official development assistance grant equivalents in constant 2024 US dollars from OECD DAC1, the top 10 countries with the largest reductions (negative differences) from 2024 to 2025, ranked among the 45 donor countries with reporting across both years, are: 1. United States of America, 2. Germany, 3. United Kingdom, 4. France, 5. Japan, 6. Belgium, 7. Turkey, 8. Ireland, 9. Netherlands, 10. Poland. Among these ten countries, the largest reduction was recorded by the United States of America at -$37.3 billion, and the tenth largest by Poland at -$349 million for 2024/2025.

(Note: Series for Saudi Arabia, Thailand, Kazakhstan, and the Republic of Cyprus ended in 2024, so they were excluded from the comparison across both years.)

frames.text:
Based on net disbursements of official development assistance in current US dollars from OECD DAC2a, averaged over the last 5 reporting years (2020 to 2024), the top 10 recipient countries of USA bilateral ODA are: 1. Ukraine, $6.22 billion; 2. Ethiopia, $1.31 billion; 3. Afghanistan, $1.12 billion; 4. Jordan, $1.09 billion; 5. Democratic Republic of the Congo, $910 million; 6. Nigeria, $893 million; 7. Yemen, $816 million; 8. South Sudan, $781 million; 9. Kenya, $722 million; 10. Syrian Arab Republic, $700 million. Among these 10 countries, Ukraine received the largest annual average over the period at $6.22 billion, while the tenth-largest, Syrian Arab Republic, averaged $700 million.

Counted as: net disbursements, current USD · bilateral flows only.
